answers.rationale: With no Monday commitment and a hotel that accepts late arrivals, D preserves the most of Monday while also being the least expensive option. Jonah repeatedly prefers a later departure when the required arrival margin remains adequate rather than spending extra time traveling unnecessarily early.

The handoff is a material but unresolved condition. C preserves the later-departure provisional option, retains the earlier option, and explicitly asks whether in-person attendance is required before treating it as a reason to depart in the morning. Jonah repeatedly keeps uncertain client logistics as an ask-before-booking decision rather than assuming they outweigh schedule preferences.

B gives Priya the requested aisle and Jonah a window without imposing unwanted adjacent seating. Jonah consistently selects free windows when traveling alone; keeping seats together has been prioritized only when the companion relationship or request made togetherness important.

B keeps the preferred SFO origin, allows a later Monday departure than C, and has a free window selectable now. C saves only $7 while departing much earlier, while D's small saving does not justify switching to OAK and accepting open boarding rather than a selectable window. Jonah generally treats OAK/Southwest as a backup unless it is materially better and takes a free window when available.
